messages_verbatim: Confirmed: implement ordinary finite JSON for the outer pinned MCP/JSON-RPC transport, independently of the integer-only public tool envelope. Keep duplicate-key/NaN/infinity rejection and exact message bounds. Preserve numeric transport identities without binary-float rounding (e.g. Decimal for outer numeric tokens with a finite JSON transport serializer), or an equally exact representation. For tools/call.arguments, serialize/reparse the actual complete sub-envelope through Core.parse_request so every decimal/exponent token remains refused even if numerically integral; transport metadata never enters policy/grants/public operation fields or bypasses closed validation. Core canonical/public serialization remains unchanged. Extended transport metadata/clientInfo/capabilities are data only, not operation authority. This implements the cited pinned MCP optional fields; it does not select a new protocol revision or public grammar. Add meaningful tests for legal transport-only decimals, rejected same values in public arguments, duplicate/nonfinite transport errors and exact RPC numeric ID roundtrip. Retain this clarification; continue.

One numeric detail: Decimal('1e0') can render as '1', which would accidentally admit an exponent token into the public integer grammar. Preserve the original numeric token class/lexeme, or ensure Decimal transport values always serialize with a decimal/exponent marker (even exact-integral Decimal values). Thus public arguments originally containing 1e0/1.0 remain rejected; ordinary JSON integer tokens remain actual ints. Add that exact discriminator.
scope: Outer pinned legacy MCP transport only; no public a_c grammar, authority or protocol-revision change
selected_realization: Preserve decimal/exponent lexemes in a finite numeric token wrapper; independently reparse the complete tools/call.arguments through Core.parse_request before any named operation.
